                                  Public Meeting Notice
                                       and Agenda
 Thursday, September 17, 2026                  10:00 AM                            Historic Courthouse
                                                                                    1616 Eighth Street
                                                                                    Minden, NV 89423


 The Board of County Commissioners sit jointly as the following boards: Liquor Board, License Board,
 Tahoe-Douglas Transportation District Board, Water District Board, and the Redevelopment Agency.
 Agenda items may be taken out of order, may be combined for consideration, or may be removed from
 the agenda at any time. All items designated “for possible action” may include discussion by the
 County Commissioners and they may take action to approve, modify, deny, take “no action,” or
 continue the item.

 To Watch the Meeting : Members of the public may click on the following link to watch the
 livestream     of      the    Board      of    County        Commissioners       meeting:
 https://www.youtube.com/@douglascountynevada

 Written Public Comment : To offer public comment before the Board meeting, members of the public
 may submit public comments online through the County’s public comment form by clicking on the
 following link:
 https://www.douglascountynv.gov/government/board_of_county_commissioners/public_comment

 Public Comment During the Meeting : Members of the public may attend the meeting in person at the
 address listed at the top of the agenda to provide public comment.

 Supporting Materials:
 Copies of supporting material can be requested in person from the Douglas County Clerk/Treasurer's
 Office, 1616 8th Street, Minden, Nevada or by calling Nicki Leeper at 775-782-9014. Electronic copies
 of the agenda and supporting materials are also available at the following websites:

 State of Nevada Public Notices Website: https://notice.nv.gov/
 Douglas County Meeting website: https://douglascountynv.granicus.com/ViewPublisher.php?
 view_id=1

 Notice to Persons with Disabilities:
 Members of the public who are disabled or require special assistance or accommodations are requested
 to notify the Douglas County Manager's Office in writing at Post Office Box 218, Minden, Nevada
 89423 or by calling 775-782-9821 at least 20 hours in advance of the meeting.

 Members of the public may call the County Manager’s office at 775-782-9821 to obtain help
 making public comment using any of the foregoing methods.

 A copy of the finalized agenda is posted at the Minden Inn at 1594 Esmeralda Avenue, Minden
 Nevada.



Douglas County Board of County Commissioners                                        September 17, 2026
                                                                                                     1

DOUGLAS COUNTY BOARD OF COUNTY COMMISSIONERS

                                           FINAL AGENDA

                                          September 17, 2026

 LUNCH BREAK
 The Board of County Commissioners may break for lunch at approximately noon and will
 reconvene after a break at the discretion of the Chairperson.

 1.   CALL TO ORDER

 2.   PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE
      Led by Commissioner Sharla Hales

 3.   PUBLIC COMMENT (No Action)
      Forum Restrictions and Orderly Conduct of Business
      The Board of County Commissioners conducts the business of Douglas County and its citizens
      during its meetings. The Board may impose reasonable, content-neutral restrictions on public
      comment such as comments that are on topics that are not within the jurisdiction, authority, or
      control of the Board of County Commissioners, or if the content of the comment is willfully
      disruptive of the meeting by being irrelevant, repetitious, slanderous, offensive, inflammatory,
      irrational, or amounts to a personal attack or interfering with the rights of other speakers. The
      presiding officer may order the removal of any person whose statement or other conduct disrupts
      the orderly, efficient or safe conduct of the meeting. Warnings against disruptive comments or
      behavior may or may not be given prior to removal. Hand clapping, making remarks or gestures
      from the audience that may interrupt, interfere or prevent any speaker from commenting should
      not occur.

      Responses to Public Comments
      The Board of County Commissioners can deliberate or take action only if a matter has been listed
      on an agenda properly posted prior to the meeting. During the public comment period, speakers
      may address matters listed or not listed on the published agenda as long as those matters are within
      the jurisdiction and control of the Board of County Commissioners. The Open Meeting Law does
      not expressly prohibit responses to public comments by the Commissioners. However, responses
      from Commissioners to unlisted public comment topics could become deliberation on a matter
      without notice to the public. On the advice of legal counsel, and to ensure the public has notice of
      all matters the Board of County Commissioners will consider, Commissioners may choose not to
      respond to public comments, except to correct factual inaccuracies, ask clarifying questions, or to
      ask that a matter be listed on a future agenda.

      Public comment is limited to three minutes per speaker unless additional time is granted by the
      Board Chairperson. The Board of Commissioners uses timing lights to ensure that everyone has
      an opportunity to speak. You will see a green light when you begin, and then a yellow light which
      indicates that you have thirty seconds left and should conclude your comments. Once the light
      turns red, please sit down.

      In addition to opening public comment, public comment will also be taken on administrative
      agenda items that are identified for possible action and closing public comment. If you plan to

Douglas County Board of County Commissioners                                           September 17, 2026
                                                                                                        2

speak on a specific agenda item that is on the administrative agenda and identified for possible
      action, then please provide your public comment when that agenda item is heard. Public
      comment will not be taken on Liquor Board agenda items. If you would like to provide public
      comment on Liquor Board agenda items, please provide your public comment during opening
      public comment or closing public comment.

      Public comment must be limited to matters that are within the jurisdiction and control of the
      Board of County Commissioners. Public comment must be addressed to the Chairperson and not
      to members of the public so that the Board may take future action on the issues that are raised by
      the public.

      At this time, public comment will be taken on those items that are within the jurisdiction and
      control of the Board of County Commissioners.

 4.   APPROVAL OF AGENDA
      For possible action. Approval of the proposed agenda. The Board of Commissioners reserves the
      right to take items in a different order to accomplish business in the most efficient manner, to
      combine two or more agenda items for consideration, and to remove items from the agenda or
      delay discussion relating to items on the agenda.

 APPROVAL OF PREVIOUS MINUTES

      5.   For possible action. Discussion to approve the minutes of the regular meeting on August 20,
           2026, of the Board of County Commissioners.

 6.   RECESS AS BOARD OF COUNTY COMMISSIONERS CONVENE AS DOUGLAS
      COUNTY LIQUOR BOARD

 DOUGLAS COUNTY LIQUOR BOARD

      7.1 For possible action. Discussion to approve adding Christy Lynn Letourneau to the existing
          Packaged Retail Liquor License for Warm Spring Road CVS, LLC, dba CVS # 7683. Christy
          Lynn Letourneau has signed a Waiver of Notice of Hearing. Warm Springs Road CVS, LLC,
          dba CVS # 7683, is located at 31 Highway 50, Suite 101, Stateline, Nevada. (Captain Koontz
          )

      7.2 For possible action. Discussion to approve the On-Site Unrestricted License and Restricted
          Gaming License for Adventure Coffee Company, dba Adventure Coffee Company,
          represented by owners Heidi Rebecca Fielek Spry and William Stanley Spry. Heidi and
          William Spry have signed a Waiver of Notice of Hearing. Adventure Coffee Company, dba
          Adventure Coffee Company, is located at 605 Highway 50, Zephyr Cove, Nevada. (Captain
          Koontz)

 8.   ADJOURN AS DOUGLAS COUNTY LIQUOR BOARD RECONVENE AS BOARD OF
      COUNTY COMMISSIONERS

 CONSENT CALENDAR
 Items appearing on the Consent Calendar are items that can be adopted with one motion unless an item
 is pulled by a Commissioner or a member of the public. Members of the public who wish to have a
 consent item placed on the Administrative Agenda shall make that request during the public comment
Douglas County Board of County Commissioners                                         September 17, 2026
                                                                                                      3

section at the beginning of the meeting and specifically state why they are making the request. If items
 are pulled for discussion by a vote of the Board of County Commissioners, they will automatically be
 placed on the Administrative Agenda to be heard at the discretion of the Chairperson or may be
 continued until another meeting.

 9.   CONSENT ITEMS

      A.   For possible action. Discussion to approve a $12,000 payment to the U.S. Army Parachute
           Team, the Golden Knights, for their parachute demonstration performance at the 2026
           Minden-Tahoe SkyFest on October 16-18, 2026, and authorize the Airport Manager to
           execute any documents necessary to complete the payment and performance arrangements
           and to approve additional expenses of up to $9,500 for the accommodations identified in the
           support manual. (Heather MacDonnell, Airport Manager)

      B.   For possible action. 1. Discussion to authorize and accept a $183,397 Federal Aviation
           Administration Airport Infrastructure Grant, with a required local match of $9,653, to design
           and construct pavement rehabilitation for the P-51 Taxilanes and authorize the County
           Manager to sign any required paperwork; and augment the Fiscal Year 2026-27 Airport
           Budget by the amount of the grant. 2. Approve Notice of Award to CR Contracting for the
           project. (Heather MacDonnell, Airport Manager)

      C.   For possible action. Discussion to approve a $28,400 service agreement with ARMOR, LLC,
           and authorize the County Manager to sign the contract and any related documents and to
           approve additional expenses of up to $7,000 as provided in the contract. The proposed
           agreement will provide Aircraft Rescue and Firefighting (ARFF), emergency response, and
           related fire and safety services for the upcoming 2026 Minden-Tahoe SkyFest Airshow on
           October 16-18, 2026. (Heather MacDonnell, Airport Manager)

      D.   For possible action. Discussion to accept a $743,490 Federal Aviation Administration
           Airport Infrastructure Grant, with a required local match of $39,132, to design and construct
           pavement rehabilitation for airport aprons; authorize the County Manager to sign any
           required paperwork; augment the Fiscal Year 2026-27 Airport Budget by the amount of the
           grant; and award the associated $631,531.50 construction contract to CR Contracting, LLC,
           and authorize the County Manager to sign the contract and approve change orders up to 10%
           of the contract amount. (Heather MacDonnell, Airport Manager)

      E.   For possible action. Discussion on the Outdoor Festival License application submitted by
           Jakota Wass for the Jakota Wass Album Release Concert to be held October 3, 2026, from
           5:30 PM to 9:45 PM, at 859 U.S. HWY 395 N., Gardnerville, Nevada. (Amy Burgans, Clerk-
           Treasurer)

      F.   For possible action. Discussion to approve a second amendment to extend the contract
           between SOE Software Corporation and Douglas County for election services, for an
           additional three (3) years, through August 25, 2029, at a total cost of $21,279; and authorize
           the Clerk-Treasurer to sign the amendment. (Amy Burgans, Clerk-Treasurer)

      G.   For possible action. Discussion to accept the cumulative voucher sheets submitted under
           NRS 244.210 for checks and electronic fund transfers issued for the 7/1/26 Payables Single,
           7/2/26 Payables, 7/10/26 Payables, 7/10/26 Payroll, 7/17/26 Payables, 7/24/26 Payables,
           7/24/26 Payroll, 7/31/26 Payables and 7/27/26 Utility Refunds. (Amy Burgans, Clerk-

Douglas County Board of County Commissioners                                          September 17, 2026
                                                                                                       4

Treasurer)

     H.   For possible action. Discussion to accept a $11,485 Workforce Recruitment and Rural
          Access Program (WRRAP) grant award to Douglas County Community Health, and
          authorize Douglas County Advanced Practice Registered Nurse Tamara Baumann to sign the
          award. (Brook Adie, Community Services Director)

     I.   For possible action. Discussion to authorize the Douglas County Weed Control Department
          to abate noxious weeds at the properties located at 959 Centerville Lane, Gardnerville,
          Nevada (APN 1220-18-001-007) and 975 Centerville Lane, Gardnerville, Nevada (APN
          1220-18-001-009) in accordance with NRS 555.170, enter into any necessary contracts
          related to the requested nuisance abatements, and to place all necessary liens on the
          properties for the cost of abatement in accordance with NRS 555.180. (Brook Adie,
          Community Services Director)

     J.   For possible action. Discussion to approve a $150,000 professional services contract with
          Kimley-Horn to prepare an update to the 2017 Douglas County Master Transportation Plan
          and authorize the County Manager to sign all necessary contract material. (Jeremy Hutchings,
          County Engineer)

     K.   For possible action. Discussion to grant a revocable license for legal access across a Douglas
          County parcel located at 3051 Heybourne Road (Assessor’s Parcel Number 1420-29-001-
          009) to Santa Ynez Valley Construction Company for the construction and maintenance of an
          access road connecting the Warm Springs Planned Development (DP22-0207) to Heybourne
          Road, as required by the conditions imposed by Douglas County for the approval of the
          Warm Springs development. (Jeremy Hutchings, County Engineer)

     L.   For possible action. Discussion to accept the auditor's report on Douglas County's general
          ledger cash balances through August 15, 2026, per Nevada Revised Statute 251.030. (Kathy
          Kaiser, Comptroller)

     M. For possible action. Discussion to approve a one-year OnBase software license and managed
        service renewal with Naviant LLC, in the amount of $67,115.11 (license & enhanced
        support) and $60,000.00 (managed services) for a total of $127,115.11, and authorize the
        Chief Information Officer to execute any required documents to complete the purchase.
        (Peace Ruggia, Chief Information Officer)

     N.   For possible action. Discussion to authorize a $276,800 professional services contract with
          Lumos & Associates to provide engineering services during the construction of the Skyline
          Tank Rehabilitation Project, and authorize the Director of Public Works to execute the
          contract and change orders up to 10% of the original contract price. (Rick Robillard, Deputy
          Public Works Director)

     O.   For possible action. Discussion to authorize a $2,780,000 construction contract with Aspen
          Developers Corp. for the Skyline Tank Rehabilitation project, and authorize the Director of
          Public Works to execute the contract and change orders up to 10% of the original contract
          price. (Rick Robillard, Deputy Public Works Director)

     P.   For possible action. Discussion to approve the purchase of one (1) motor pool vehicle from
          Corwin Ford, for a total of $37,528.25, for Fiscal Year 2026-27 under Nevada State Contract
          99SWC-NV26-25906, and authorize the Public Works Director to sign all required

                                                                                                      5

documents. (Jeff MacDonnell, Fleet and Facilities Manager)

      Q.   For possible action. Discussion to approve a $75,000 purchase order with Ozone Water
           Systems, Inc. for the replacement, repair, rental, and maintenance of the ozone disinfection
           system at the the ZWUD Water Surface Treatment Plant; and authorize the Director of Public
           Works to execute the purchase order. (Rick Robillard, Deputy Public Works Director)

 ADMINISTRATIVE AGENDA
 The Chairperson will read the agenda title into the public record and will have the discretion to
 determine how the item will be presented. Agenda items may be considered ahead of or after the
 schedule indicated by this agenda. Public comment will be taken on items that are identified for possible
 action.

 10. ITEM(S) PULLED FROM THE CONSENT AGENDA WILL BE HEARD AT THIS TIME

 PRESENTATIONS

      11.1 For presentation only. Ceremonial presentation of Proclamation 2026P-054 designating the
           week of October 4-10, 2026, as National 4-H Week in Douglas County, Nevada. (Christel
           Passink, 4-H & Youth Development Instructor)

      11.2 For presentation only. Ceremonial presentation of Proclamation 2026P-053 designating the
           week of September 20-26, 2026, as National Community Emergency Response Team Week
           in Douglas County, Nevada. (Kara Easton, Emergency Management Director)

 COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT

      12.1 For possible action. Discussion to adopt Resolution 2026R-051, a resolution of the Douglas
           County Board of Commissioners granting $20,000 of Douglas County public funds to Main
           Street Gardnerville for the Business Facade Improvement Grant Program; approve a grant
           agreement for Fiscal Year 2026-27 between Douglas County and Main Street Gardnerville
           establishing the terms of the $20,000 grant; and authorize the Community Development
           Director to execute the grant agreement. (Jen Tune, Main Street Gardnerville Executive
           Director; and Andrea Pawling, Deputy Community Development Director)

      12.2 For presentation only. Presentation on the 2027 Federal Housing and Urban Development
           Community Development Block Grant (CDBG) program to include a summary of potential
           projects and outreach to the community for the 2027 grant cycle. (Linda Doherty, Assistant
           Planner)

      12.3 For possible action. Discussion of Appeal 2026-APPEAL-0003, an appeal of the Planning
           Commission's decision to deny Appeal 2026-APPEAL-0002, upholding the Community
           Development staff's decision to approve Major Design Review DP25-0184, for a Developed
           Campground with 53 campsites to include 26 cabins/sleeping shelters, nine (9) tree house
           structures (on the ground), 18 seasonal dome structures, and three (3) comfort stations
           (bathrooms/showers). The project also includes a clubhouse for guest use (including a
           communal kitchen, edible garden, digital nomad space, conference room, communal eating
           area, and educational wall) and one accessory dwelling to be used to house up to nine
           employees. The subject property is located in the S-070B (Sports-oriented in the Rabe
           Community Plan Area) in the Tahoe Basin, near the southwesterly intersection of Elks Point

Douglas County Board of County Commissioners                                          September 17, 2026
                                                                                                       6

Road and Highway 50. The appellant is G&T Properties LLC and the appellant’s
          representative is Samantha Vanillo of Womble Bond Dickinson LLP. The original applicant
          for the Design Review is Jamie Schmidt of JLS-Development, on behalf of Globetrotters
          Property LLC (property owner). APN 1318-22-001-013. (Linda Doherty, Assistant Planner)

     12.4 For possible action. Discussion regarding the adoption of Resolution 2026R-048, a
          resolution amending and establishing certain rates, fees, and charges for services provided by
          the Douglas County Community Development Department as provided for in the Douglas
          County Code, proposing a 5.1% increase to the 2026 Community Development Schedule on
          November 1, 2026, and repealing Resolution 2024R-053, which established and amended the
          rates, fees, and charges for the Department set in 2024. The proposed increases are based on
          the Western Urban Consumer Price Index's (CPI) combined increase over the past two years
          (2025 & 2026). (Tom Dallaire, Community Development Director and Andrea Pawling,
          Deputy Community Development Director)

     12.5 For possible action. Discussion regarding the adoption of Resolution 2026R-052, a
          resolution adopting the 2026 fee adjustments for commercial and residential building permits
          pursuant to Title 20, Appendix B, Intentional Building Code section 109, International
          Residential Code section R108, and NRS section 354.598981; and repealing Resolution
          2021R-107, which formerly established and amended the rates, fees, and charges for the
          Department in 2021. Community Development recommends an increase in the Fee Schedule
          by 5.1% on November 1, 2026, based on the Western Urban Consumer Price Index's (CPI)
          combined increase over the past two years (2025 & 2026). (Tom Dallaire, Community
          Development Director and Andrea Pawling, Deputy Community Development Director)

     12.6 For possible action. Discussion regarding the adoption of Resolution 2026R-016, a
          resolution amending certain rates, fees, and charges for services provided by the Douglas
          County Community Development, Vacation Home Rental (VHR) Department, as provided
          for in Douglas County Code 20.622, and repealing Resolution 2022R-089, which previously
          established the current VHR fees in 2022. Community Development recommend an increase
          in the Fee Schedule by approximately 15% on November 1, 2026. These increases are based
          on the Board of County Commissioners' desire to have the VHR program be self-funded.
          (Tom Dallaire, Community Development Director and Ernie Strehlow, Program Manager)

 COUNTY MANAGER

     13. For presentation only. Announcements/reports/updates from County Commission members,
         including updates on the various boards and/or commissions that they may be a member of or
         a liaison to, or any other meetings/functions they have attended, and any request by a
         Commissioner for discussion of a future agenda item. (Chairman Gardner)

 14. CLOSING PUBLIC COMMENT (No Action)
     At this time, public comment will be taken on those items that are within the jurisdiction and
     control of the Board of Commissioners or those agenda items where public comment has not
     already been taken.

 15. ADJOURNMENT
